answer: A newcomer earns a seat by ringing one sparrow at a named karst sinkhole: a licensed ringer fits a numbered basalt ring to the bird's leg and releases it, while two watchers log the flight the same day; a ring found reused, or a bird never logged, voids the claim and burns a 500 POA bond. Each ringing costs a $120 ringer fee plus an $80 ring, so 100 fakes need 100 rings, $20,000 in fees and 50,000 POA in bonds, while honest ringers track real birds.
